newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open higher Friday in line with further gains in the bullion market overnight as the dollar slid to a six-week low against the yen and four-week low against the mark.

Part of the reason for the fall in gold in the past year to a four-year low had been the steady rise in the dollar, making gold more expensive in many currencies, but this may now be reversed, analysts said.
COMEX June gold was called up $0.50 to $1.00 from the previous close of $344.80 an ounce.
COMEX gold stocks were unchanged at 910,877 ounces Thursday.
Spot gold was quoted at $344.80/$345.30 early compared to the London morning fix of $343.75 -- the highest in three weeks. In New York Thursday, spot gold ended quoted at $343.50/$344.00.
COMEX July silver was called unchanged to up 0.5 cent from the previous close of $4.836 after trading from $4.84 to $4.875 on ACCESS.
COMEX silver stocks fell 1,218,679 ounces Thursday to 191,367,744 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum and June palladium were called up $0.50 to $1.00 from their prior closes of $379.50 and 157.90, respectively.
In London today, palladium was fixed at its highest in in nearly two years at $162.50.
